February 2, 2028

Order 9656 signed, Danny San.

50% tariffs on imports and exports except for countries in THEP, EEPH, EEDA, or PETROX
Closed the border to almost all immigration allowing only 100 individuals each week.
The requirement of all buildings to fly a standard issue Western View flag that is sent to all buildings. If a standard issue flag is not produced after 3 warnings that will arrive in the mail in 1 week increments then a fine can be forced that can be up to 1,000,000 Westerns. If the flag is damaged or vandalized a similar fine can be produced. If a person has received multiple fines they could be sent to jail for treason, or if they are a second citizen (a citizen from another country that has gotten their citizenship or other permission to stay in Western View) then they can be deported back to their original country.
All private industry is banned.
Tax increased to 50% for middle class but those with more money or people who have worked more than 10 years in the government have only a 45% income tax.
All citizens ages 16-60 are required to work in some job for the government for at least 10 years, this includes military service. Those who don't can be fined or sent to jail.
The death penalty is legal and can be forced upon somebody by the Head Council but if it is forced upon someone they could pay 10,000 Westerns to the government to have their original sentence.
The police are now fully commanded by the Head Council.
Any decision the Council of 13 makes can be overruled by the Head Council and 1 of the Council of 13.

[quote=montfleur;61681659][b]I give them 10 days[/b]

Belgarde has surrendered to the joint expeditionary forces, stated Eleonore, walking into Henris office.

That is good, replied Henri setting down the phone having just gotten off a call, Do you know who that was?

Eleonore nodded, No,

That was the duc of Thýven, he wants some military backing to knock out an SCSID installation in his region, he says that the people are ready to secede as soon as the duc of Knygta and Deyn gives them the green light, replied Henri.

Eleonore nodded once more, And why is Knygta and Deyn waiting?

They want Montfleur to send some protection into the White Sea, in case the regime decides to be funny, replied Henri, leaning back, How long do you think we would have to wait if we activated part of our reserve fleet and a few frigates for this? 

Eleonore thought for a few minutes, If we scrambled, a day or two, depending on what ships already are able to be piloted? 

Henri nodded, My biggest concern is the Rosenmarkket sub fleet, intel is unsure on their crews, Begren played hard with them apparently, kept them in line,

Eleonore, I can look into it sir, I doubt theyd have the capacity to raise their entire submarine fleet, 

I want airstrikes, on the major docks, the submarine docks, stated Henri bluntly.

The SAM systems on the Rosenmarkket coastline is dense and well, even battered it produced some force against the Wuloosyans, replied Eleonore.

Lets look then at our options, replied Henri, Use strikes as a last resort, can we get Wuloosya in on this? 

I can check, replied Eleonore.

Good, nodded Henri, pulling out his VicodinEle from a drawer and popping one into his mouth.

[b]August 10, 2028: The long decline[/b]
[b]An Address to the Nation by Haakon Strømm[/b]

My fellow citizens, 

The nation is stronger than ever before, the fascist powers that have attempted to take over Belgarde have only perceived the sight of victory. The traitors who gave the state to our enemy shall be sought out and done justice to! The Eternal Revolution is stable! Order shall be restored, I am the Consul of Order! I myself have won the war against the Montfleurois and the Wuloosyans! We will win! Order shall be restored!

And upon that glorious day when the enemies of Rosenmarkke are cast asunder! I shall seek out reforms like never before! We will raise the pensions of our soldiers! Increase spending on social services! Everything shall be done in the name of our people! We will defend the integrity of the state, the nation, the ideology of Strømmism!

[b]Crisis[/b]

Thýven has just announced their secession, sir, stated Eleonore as she rushed into the situation room where Henri had gathered his staff to discuss potential strikes against the Rosenmarkket navy.

Have they? asked Henri, I assume they are sending a delegate post haste then, replied Henri, referring to the invitations he had sent out to the various seceding regions to send delegates to discuss unification.

They have, uh, a Iosep Østens? replied Eleonore, as she checked her notes.

Ah, Iosef Broz Østens, a former member of the Council of 99, a very well-rounded man, smiled Henri with a gleam in his eye. 

Yes, him, replied Eleonore, What do we have for Knygta and Deyn? 

James Wellton, some local official, I couldnt figure it out, replied Henri dismissively, Not a well known figure,

I see, has Westmarkke made any calls recently? Asked Eleonore.

Yes, they have signalled their intent, Thýven intends to push them furtherdid you see the speech by Haakon? asked Henri.

Yes, it was driveling madness, replied Eleonore.

I still give this regime 9 days? Maybe less, I meanpeople are massing in the capital city, and the soldiers not loyal to the regime, they wont fire on their own citizens, replied Henri.

What is the situation with the strikes? asked Eleonore, sitting down to look at the map that had been pulled up.

We are looking at striking one of their older ships, the last Cold War  frigate they have, replied Henri.

I can sign off on this, replied Eleonore, Itll send a message, 

Ah, so now you want strikes, the other day you didnt! chortled Henri.

On the subs, I am against striking the subs, replied Eleonore.

Ah, well, waved Henri, The subs, we will be striking those too, we know they are uncrewed, unmanned, and frankly stuck in the dock. 

WHAT? asked Eleonore as General Charles Martel de Funes entered the room to give an operational report.

Sir, began the general, We are ready to commit to the strikes, our forces are ready to send in ground troops as soon as we get the all clear from our forces in Belgarde,

You may proceed, nodded Henri. The general saluted and went out of the room to give the final orders.

Henri, if this screws us, Ill began Eleonore before being cut off, Ill take the responsibilty, he smiled.

[b]August 12, 2028: 9:00 AM, The Bombing of Tharkønn[/b]

Haakon Strømm was awoken by the sound of explosions shaking the governor's palace and rattling the window. Rising from the bed, he shouted, Theyre attacking! Theyre attacking! as some officers rushed into the room upon the sound of his cries.

We must get to the bunker! He declared as he moved with the guards down the halls of the mansion, a dull roar could be heard beyond the walls.

As they were walking, Begren and his own staff appeared. 

Begren, what is going on?! Who is bombing? Is it the Wuloosyans! Demanded Haakon, grabbing Begrens arm.

Sir we need to secure you, replied Begren.

Secure me for what? He asked as they rushed down a staircase.

An attack has been launched on this city by a coalition of secessionists and the Montfleurois government, replied Begren calmly.

What is that roar I hear? Are those my people? Asked Haakon.

There are protestors in the square, the soldiers have a perimeter around the building, replied Begren.

I must see them, my people! Cried Haakon, breaking away from the group and heading towards the state sitting room where the balcony facing the square was.

Follow him, muttered Begren, The fool, 

Haakon rushed into the room, ran to the doors and flung them open, stepping out into the bright morning sun as the full roar of the crowd hit him. Television cameras had begun to film.

Citizens, comrades! He declared waving to the protesting crowd, I welcome you! He pumped both fists, Begren and the guards had entered the room, Dear comrades, citizens of the capital, I wish to address the great achievements of the Strømmist construction! The shouts grew louder as the crowd surged forward, The state is winning! The state is winning! The state is winning! He declared with a wave of his hand, loud booms in the harbor shook the square, The terrorists will not win, the fascist forces will not win! The foreign interference in Belgarde, Thýven, Knygta and Deyn, and across this nation is being crushed and will be crushed, at this point Begren had come out onto the balcony to try to pull Haakon into the palace. Another boom shook the square as dark smoke began to fill the sky, Friends! Friends! Sit! Sit! Let us be calm! This is a provocation! This is treason! Continued Haakon dazed as he tapped the microphone and motioned for the crowd to calm, Unity! Order! We shall establish order! Cried Haakon as Begren finally managed to yank him into the palace to the cheers of the crowd which surged forward once more.

What are you doing?! Demanded Haakon, I am chief consul, these are my people! 

We need to get you somewhere safe, we need to leave the capital, declared Begren as he moved Haakon once more through the halls to a waiting underground garage

Where is my wife? Where is my wife? He asked.

Eliza is at the airport, with the jet sir, replied one of the aides as they pushed him into the car and began to drive.

The car twisted and turned across the streets of the city, attempting to avoid the protesters who were in the streets, a preplanned evacuation route had been made utilising utility roads.

Upon arriving at the airport, Haakon was rushed out of the car and onto a waiting government jet where he embraced his wife, The state! The state! He declared, Its lost, Ive lost the state, he began to blubber as he sat down, Eliza squeezing his hand gently as the plane taxied down the runway.

[b] 10:30 AM: The grand victory[/b]

Sir we have recieved reports that the governors palace in Tharkønn has been taken, began General Charles Martel de Funes,

What? Thats excellent? By whom? Asked Henri, leaping up from his seat.

Protestors, replied de Funes.

And what of the Strømms? Asked Henri.

They are believed to have fled, but we will be in contact with whatever nation they fly over to attempt to force a landing, we believe they may be flying to Montesqiue, 

The island that is several thousand kilometers away? Asked Henri incredulously, Theyll never make it!

That is not a concern right now, the army awaits your orders, 

Alright, alright, I want the ducs in Rosenmarkke contacted immediately, I want their delegates that are already here summoned immediately, and uh, get ready for a trip to Tharkønn, spewed off Henri in rapid succession.

How long will we have to get to Tharkønn? asked Henri.

By plane 3 or 4 hours, replied the general, By train about eight, he stated.

Can we get a stop in Belgarde? asked Henri.

Yes, replied the general.

Excellent, so what 9 hour train ride to Tharkønn, how long to get troops on the ground in the city? Asked Henri.

Well, given our readiness at this moment, the gendarme could probably have it ready in four maybe five hours if we scramble, replied the General.

Excellent, lets do that, I want whomever we have in Mittlemarkke to establish connections and begin rapid coordination of the ground situation, I know loyalists are going to be attempting to take back the palace and the city, continued Henri, popping a Vicodin.

The Rosenmarkket border had been closed following the initial secession of Knygta and Deyn, guarded by a chain-link fence and concrete wall. Built in 1970 as a device for national defense, the border had become neglected in the 90s and early 2000s as the government of Rosenmarkke focused on more internal matters.

Immediately, the group began to try to break the gate down, which was locked into place by an automatic lock switch that was not anywhere near the area.
